purpose: Tafluprost is used to lower the pressure inside your eye. It is prescribed for conditions like glaucoma or ocular hypertension, where the pressure in your eye is too high. Keeping that pressure under control helps protect your vision and prevents damage to the optic nerve.
how_it_works: Your eye constantly produces a fluid called aqueous humor. In glaucoma, this fluid does not drain properly, causing pressure to build up. Tafluprost works by helping that fluid drain out of your eye more easily, which lowers the pressure and keeps your eye healthier.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is eye redness or irritation after putting in the drops. You may also notice your eye itching, feeling dry, or watering more than usual. Over time, some people notice their eyelashes getting longer, thicker, or darker, and the colored part of the eye or the skin around the eye may gradually become darker — let your doctor know if you notice this.
warnings: Do not use this medication while wearing contact lenses — wait at least 15 minutes after putting in the drops before putting your lenses back in. Tell your doctor if you have had eye surgery or any eye inflammation. If you use other eye drops, wait at least 5 minutes between each one. Avoid getting the drops on your skin regularly, as it may cause darkening. Keep it out of reach of children. If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, talk to your doctor before using this medication.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one drop into the affected eye or eyes once daily, in the evening. Using it at the same time each day works best. Do not use it more than once a day, as that can actually make it less effective.
